en: Likewise, I'm sure.
Until we meet again. Good day.
I'm on my way to work now. Goodbye.
Good morning. You're up early.
I'm off to work now, so see you later.
It's me, Winifred!
How lovely to see you so early in the day.
Today's going to be a good day, I just know it.
Good evening, miss.
I wonder if I might ask the way
Oh, good evening.
Certainly. Where are you headed?
I heard there was a bank around here
The banks are in the City district.
But it's evening already and they're closed,
so why not go tomorrow?
Thank you for your kindness, miss.
It's Winifred.
Very well, Winifred.
. Please call me that.
note: After #525 'I am ' + name. JP is 'Please call me {NAME}'; better if #525 gets a variant 'Please call me ' for msg 275300 and this row becomes '.'

en: Thank you for the directions. Until next time.
Good day...
Are you keeping well?
I don't know what your work is,
but you always seem so busy.
Do keep it up.
Good evening. We meet again today.
What brings you out tonight?
<I'm meeting someone>
<A night stroll>
Oh, meeting someone? How lovely.
I'm so busy with work
I never get a chance to meet anyone.
I envy you.
note: After #152 '...', then pause and #6914 on the same line.

en: Well, until next time.
What a lovely pastime.
I should stop living only for my work, too,
and take some time for myself.
Oh? Hello, may I help you?
For telephone inquiries, see the counter.
Hello. Is this place off-limits, then?
My apologies. I seem to have lost my way.
Oh, well, if you're lost, it can't be helped.
This is the telephone operators' room.
The counter is on the other side.
Thank you, fair lady.
I would very much like to know your name.
My, what a flatterer.
I'm Winifred. Pleased to meet you.
I'll remember your name. Good day.
Oh? I'm afraid you can't come in here.
Oh, it's you! What brings you here?
Ah, hello. So this is where you work.
I'm sorry, I got rather lost.
I work as a telephone operator.
This is the operators' room, you see.
The counter is on the other side.
Thank you. Until later, then.
You know where the counter is by now, don't you?
Oh? ...Oh, dear.
You mustn't come in here.
Pardon me.
I wanted to see you, so I couldn't help myself.
W-why! Please don't joke like that.
Goodness, what am I to say to that?
I have work to do, so... another time.
Have you come by again?
What can I do for you today?
Could it be you're teasing me?
Still, I'm a little glad you came.
I've no complaints, but nothing ever changes.
Hello. How are you today?
Coming to see an old maid like me,
you really are a strange one.
note: Lowercase: follows #6952 (comma) and #7012 (should end with a comma).

en: I've thrown myself into my work
Is marriage a woman's happiness after all?
Or is it love itself, I wonder?
Hello, is anyone there?
Yes, who is it?
Um... did you want something from me?
